questions.content:
Explain whether each of the following constitutes data collected from population or a sample.

a.  Opinions on a certain issue obtained from all adults living in a city.

b.  The price a gallon of regular unleaded gasoline on a given day at each of 35 gas stations in the Miami, Florida, metropolitan area.

c.  Credit card debts of 100 families selected from San Antonio, Texas.

d.  The percentage of all U.S. registered voters in each state who voted in 2012 Presidential election.

e.  The number of left-handed students in each of 50 classes selected from a given university.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment and solution_Chap 1&2.docx

questions.content:
Classify each statement as true or false.

a. A population is the complete set of units about which a study seeks information.

b. Examining only some population units constitutes a census.

c. A quantitative variable is also called a categorical variable.

d. Statistical inference uses sample measurements to generalize about a population.

e. Describing the important features of a set of measurements is called statistical inference.

questions.content:
Below we list several variables. Which of these variables are quantitative and which are qualitative? Explain.

a\. The dollar amount on an accounts receivable invoice.

b\. The net profit for a company in 2005.

c\. The stock exchange on which a company's stock is traded.

d\. The national debt of the United States in 2005.

e\. The advertising medium (radio, television, or print) used to promote a product.
